## Open

### F-168 — IPivotConfig declared type contradicted the implementation

> _2026-09-16 · core/blong · open_

The public IPivotConfig declared join as a descriptor triple and required it, while TableWidget
treats join as an optional map of pivot key to data key (`Record<pivotKey, dataKey>`, e.g.
`{value: entityId, label: entityName}`) and never reads the descriptor fields. Fixed the type to
match; no consumer broke because realm models pass widget.pivot through the loose IWidgetOverride. A
new `defaults?: Record<string, unknown>` was added so a pivot slot with no stored data can seed
non-join fields (a tri-state cell that must start as inherit - unedited pivot slots are never
submitted).

### F-648 — The contract package cannot re-export a value beside its types

> _2026-10-30 · core/blong · open_

Putting two small runtime helpers in the chat contract looked like the tidy home for them — one
formatter of an answer's words and one reader of the id a send reply names, shared by the realm and
both ports. It cannot work: `core/blong` is the one package that _emits_ (`heft build` → `dist`,
`module: NodeNext`) and its tsconfig has no `allowImportingTsExtensions` because that option
requires `noEmit`, so a value re-export through `'./chat.ts'` fails TS5097 while the type-only
`export type * from './chat.ts'` beside it is fine, the specifier never reaching emit. The runtime
needs exactly the opposite: the package's `./types` export maps to the source `types.ts`, and Node's
type stripping resolves a `.ts` specifier but not a `.js` one, so the two requirements cannot both
be met by an import. The commit hook caught it as the last step of a finished change; the fix was to
move both helpers back to the realm and carry the rendered answer to the ports as a field
(`answerText`) instead of a function. The lesson is that this package's shared surface is types
only, and that a helper belongs where it is _used_ — one caller can compute a string, while a port
that had to derive it would carry a formatter for a contract it only displays.
